sentence: This project studies how histone expression changes in the aging retinal pigment epithelium and how it affects cell death and age-related macular degeneration.
This project uses gene therapy to give vein grafts an atheroprotective molecule and tests it in animal models of vein graft failure.
This project studies the cells and circuits behind spatial learning and how it relates to dopamine release during body movements.
This project uses complex natural products called terpenoids as a starting point to develop prototype chemotherapeutics for cancer.
This project explores how taste and smell work and how the brain circuits involved relate to obesity, eating disorders and hypertension.
This project tests a radiotracer for neuroimaging and studies how its target relates to alcohol seeking and consumption in people with alcohol use disorder.
This project studies how ketone bodies help keep polyunsaturated fatty acids balanced in the liver and how that affects liver disease.
This project uses the simple model organism Caenorhabditis elegans to find genes that control long-lasting changes in the nervous system caused by drugs.
This project expands the laboratory's ability to work on infectious diseases including Mycobacterium tuberculosis and influenza.
This project studies how T cells can stay effective and avoid exhaustion during chronic viral infection.
This project uses single-cell technologies to study how immune responses in elite controllers recognize and eliminate HIV reservoir cells.
This project builds ways to study how many genes at once affect human health and disease.
This project tracks where and when key biochemical activities of an actin assembly complex happen inside living cells using microscopy and genetics.
This project studies how microRNA released by breast cancer cells changes normal cells in the brain to help cancer spread there.
This project studies how different metalloenzyme families control their use of metal ions and the outcomes of their reactions.
This project studies how a genetic abnormality in a cancer driver gene affects signaling in human T-cell lymphomas.
This project studies how alcohol changes protein signaling and activity in the liver through changes to cysteine and lysine.
This project builds precise motor measures using digital technologies to tell if a therapy works in children with ataxia-telangiectasia.
This project studies how methylglyoxal, a toxic metabolic by-product, damages DNA and disrupts repair in obesity-linked prostate cancer.
This project studies how cells divide, grow and respond to stress differently in tissues, focusing on the endocycle and a tumor suppressor.
